scope: Source questions recorded at restoration commit 07d40c4; author resolutions are recorded below and implemented through separately reviewed author amendments.

questions.section: 17. A Forward Assignment Is a Debt / 十七、前指是债
questions.finding: The Chinese passage attributes explicit prospect-essay handovers to prequel, ep02 and ep03. These exact handovers were not found in the current local website bodies or by git log -S 展望篇 for those files. ep01 unit204 does explicitly assign action to 展望篇; ep04 does assign it to 行动论. The passage may refer to another paper version rather than these published website bodies.
questions.resolution: The author identifies the prospect as academic Value Theory Paper 0. Academic prequel/P2/P3 all contain the handovers; the prose adaptation omitted them. Preserve the historical argument and explicitly identify its academic referents.
questions.original_author_question: Identify the source versions being cited, or authorize a substantive source correction. Translations currently preserve the Chinese passage faithfully.

questions.finding: Chinese refers to 第四格里「门在而弃用」, although the four cases above list that state second. French already uses a neutral back-reference, but other editions may reproduce the ordinal.
questions.classification: Likely minor cross-reference typo; not a substantive doctrinal change.
questions.resolution: Correct fourth to second where that ordinal occurs; retain already-correct neutral references in other editions.

questions.finding: The Chinese explicitly says 判断力 occurs zero times in the seven body essays. It occurs in ep04 unit135 and ep05 unit89, both as handovers to action theory. The adjacent claim that the faculty is not developed as an independent explanatory mechanism may still be correct.
questions.resolution: Replace the zero-occurrences claim with the narrower claim: the faculty appears in handover passages but is not developed as an independent explanatory mechanism.
questions.original_author_question: Clarify whether 正文 excludes these handover passages, or authorize changing the literal zero-occurrences statement to the narrower not-developed claim.
